title: BEETLE:BIT · Week 9 · Build, Check & Code
wagba: Complete one secure assembly step OR upload and explain a working program.
objective:
Knowledge: micro:bit inputs, outputs and the REKA:BIT motor controller.
Skills: match parts, check joints, read blocks, upload and observe.
Understanding: pause waits while motors run; brake stops them. An app tick is not permission to power a robot.
keywords: inspect · input · output · upload · pause · brake
challenge: Explain one real result, then predict the effect of changing just one thing.

rows.screen: Own labelled box · all power disconnected
students: Open Week 9. Match your actual robot to the right route.
Keep loose parts in your own working tray.
rows.build: Choose your assembly and exact booklet step. Do not restart automatically.
rows.code: Open Coding Lab. Keep motor power disconnected, including the twin cable’s barrel plug.
rows.teacher: Welcome pupils, open the Week 9 app and sort the room into Build Bench or Coding Lab. Ask each pair to point to their actual next step.
rows.check: No assumed completion: inspect the real build. A simulator program or a finished-looking robot is not proof of readiness for power.
rows.support: Before pupils arrive: bench-test the forward 100 / pause 500 ms / brake example on your kit; prepare known data cables, labelled parts trays, correct batteries, a secure raised-wheel support and a marked floor lane. Swap builder/checker roles at the next work block.

students: Show where power is disconnected before adjusting anything.
Show Mr Kang any missing or faulty screws or bolts.
rows.build: Match the fixing to the photo and measure the real part. Never force a poor fit.
rows.code: Buttons A/B are inputs; LEDs and motors are outputs. Teacher approval comes before motor power.
rows.teacher: Model power-off handling and one correct fixing. Triage missing or damaged parts now; pupils show you their report and the actual part or empty fixing position.
rows.check: Record part type, quantity, booklet step and kit label so replacements or purchases can be arranged. The long motor fixing size is unconfirmed; a smooth brass hex body alone is not a fault.
rows.support: Reports stay on each pupil’s browser: saving one does not notify you. Keep a teacher parts list without publishing pupil data. No borrowing from another kit, no force-tightening and no powered wiring changes.

students: Read or watch the guide for your current step.
Predict what should happen before you test.
rows.build: Find → Watch if helpful → Build → physically Check. Keep the battery and USB out.
rows.code: Make the display project: start = square, A = heart, B = tick. Test in the simulator.
rows.teacher: Circulate once to unblock starts. Help builders identify the correct fixing; point coders to the actual MakeCode screenshots rather than building the program for them.
rows.check: Every pair can name one achievable goal and find the relevant guide. Stop and flag an uncertain fixing instead of improvising.
rows.support: Booklet fixing mismatches are flagged in the app. Use the matching image and actual components; do not tell the whole class to use an unverified substitute. While awaiting help, compare pictures or practise code with motor power off.

students: Keep working on your own small goal.
If stuck, check the photo or use Parking Lab while waiting.
rows.build: Complete and inspect one joint. Keep unused fixings in the labelled box.
rows.code: Finish the LED program. Use the app’s USB upload guide; leave all motor barrel plugs out.
rows.teacher: Sit where you can see the room. Take a quieter supervision window; keep the powered-test area closed and avoid starting a help queue. Respond immediately to safety concerns.
rows.check: Only assembly and display/screen practice. Pupils waiting for inspection use the simulator or Parking Lab; nobody self-authorises motor power.
rows.support: This is seated supervision, not leaving the class unsupervised. Invite only urgent safety or trapped-part concerns now. Bring non-urgent questions to the 08:55 check station. Micro:bit USB may run an old program, so wheels remain clear and motor supply disconnected.

rows.screen: One robot at a time · teacher-led tests only
students: Bring the actual joint or exact code question to the check station.
Keep working without motor power while you wait.
rows.build: Show the joint, orientation and clearance on your actual robot.
rows.code: Prove the real micro:bit shows heart on A and tick on B. Only inspected robots try motor checks.
rows.teacher: Stay seated at the check station. Inspect one robot at a time: fixings, wiring, battery polarity and cable clearance. Supervise raised-wheel motor checks only when you can give full attention.
rows.check: Compare M1A, M1B, M2A and M2B with booklet p.38. Stop for a jam, wrong direction or unexpected behaviour; disconnect all power before correction.
rows.support: Do not open a second powered station or run a floor test while helping a builder. Do not rush all coders to motors: a successful display upload is a valid outcome. This is a seated teaching window, not a rest break.

students: Show your partner one piece of evidence.
Swap builder/checker or driver/navigator roles.
rows.build: Choose the next unfinished step or repair the joint that failed its check.
rows.code: Read the movement stacks: startup brake; A = move 100 → pause 500 ms → brake; B = brake.
rows.teacher: Make a short room sweep and reset the test area to closed. Ask for one precise check or observation, then assign each pair a manageable next step.
rows.check: Check code comprehension: pause does not stop the motors; the brake after it does. B is a programmed brake, not a safety-rated emergency switch.
rows.support: New movement project: Beetlebit-W9-MoveStop, with Cytron’s ZOOMBIT extension added to that project too. REKA:BIT is the red controller; do not mix this lesson’s blocks with an older direct-REKA:BIT example.

rows.screen: Test area closed · motor supply disconnected
students: Use one example to improve one thing.
Record a prediction before your next test.
rows.build: Build or repair one small section, then compare it with the photo.
rows.code: Build and save the movement program without motor power, or play the screen-only Parking Lab.
rows.teacher: Sit and observe the whole room for a second quieter window. Keep robot motor power off and defer non-urgent hands-on help until the 09:20 station.
rows.check: No unattended motor or gripper test. The Parking Lab is a virtual programming game; its distances do not predict real robot travel.
rows.support: Pupils save their MakeCode .hex and keep a known-working display project. If a pupil has an unresolved hardware fault, move them to LED/simulator work; do not make a power test the reward for finishing early.

rows.screen: Teacher checks code · press A once · wait for stop
students: Show all three code stacks before connecting motor power.
Observe one short movement, then switch off before adjustments.
rows.build: Continue your actual assembly. A secure step is a successful checkpoint.
rows.code: Teacher-led raised-wheel test first. Floor lane only with permission; unplug the computer tether.
rows.teacher: Supervise one test at a time. Inspect startup brake, A’s timed move and B’s brake; test raised wheels first. Open the marked floor lane only if you can supervise it directly.
rows.check: Starting settings: speed 100/255, pause 500 ms, brake. Use your bench-tested kit settings; stop a stall or unexpected movement. Keep physical power control available and hands away from moving parts.
rows.support: The station is seated if the setup allows a clear view and safe reach; stand for a floor test when needed. After a successful checked test, approve changing only 500 → 750 ms and ask for a prediction. Gripper is video preview only until you have calibrated it; no unchecked 0°/180° commands.

rows.screen: Stop motors · explain evidence, not speed
students: Show one secure build check or working program.
Explain what happened and name your next step.
rows.build: Point to the actual joint you checked and any unfinished section.
rows.code: Explain the real LED or movement result. Early finishers improve a Parking Lab program.
rows.teacher: Sit at the evidence station and listen to short pair explanations. Accept a secure assembly, a real display upload or a checked motor result; students need not all reach the same milestone.
rows.check: Distinguish simulator evidence from a real-board upload. Collect any unresolved part type, quantity, step and kit label for replacement or purchasing follow-up.
rows.support: No new powered test during this explanation window. A curved drive is useful evidence, not automatic failure: battery, surface and motor differences matter. Extension planning may continue on screen without powered autonomous driving.

rows.screen: All power disconnected · own labelled box
students: Switch off and unplug motor power and USB. Save your work.
Pack your own parts and leave a precise note for next time.
rows.build: Save the actual next booklet step. Put loose fixings in the labelled tray or box.
rows.code: Save the MakeCode .hex and separate Week 9 progress backup in school files.
rows.teacher: Check all robots are off and disconnected. Confirm labelled boxes, protected cables and grippers, saved files and a clear floor. Finish by 09:50.
rows.check: Each pair can state one next action. Make sure pupils have actually shown you their missing-parts report; the app does not send it automatically.
rows.support: Keep pupil backups and teacher parts lists private, outside the public GitHub folder. Browser progress and the MakeCode .hex are different things. Do not manually force servo jaws into a packing position.
